text.p: - The first session of the new Slovenian parliament, scheduled for Thursday, will be headed by the oldest member of the assembly, the Christian Democrats' Marijan Schiffrer.
- Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun will visit Estonia on Monday and Tuesday to sign a free-trade agreement with the Baltic state.

- The United List of Social Democrats, the former communist party, is expected to change leadership at its congress in February following its poor result in this month's general elections. The party got nine parliamentary seats, down from 14 four years ago.
- Slovenian electricity companies push for higher electricity prices to enable them to raise investment outlays.
- Workers of troubled shoe producer Peko threatened to go on strike unless they received their October saleries by the end of November.
- Health insurance company ZZZS said 1.11 percent of the country's output was used for medicines last year, up from 0.53 percent in 1990.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek will start coalition talks with all parliamentary parties this week.

- Foreign ministers of the European Union (EU) countries are expected to pass a temporary trade agreement with Slovenia in Brussels on Monday. The agreement will go into effect in January and be in force until the association accord with Slovenia is ratified by all EU members.
